transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (NovaPay CTO), Elena Ruiz (NovaPay ML), Jordan Lee (NovaPay Infra), Marta Gomez (NovaPay PM)

[00:00] Alex Chen: All right everyone, thanks for hopping on. Uh, quick check — is everyone on the right calendar invite?
[00:05] Samir Patel: Yep, all good. We've got about 40 minutes, right?
[00:08] Alex Chen: Yep, 40ish. Agenda — quick recap of last week's runs, Priya will walk through TTFT numbers, then dive into streaming behaviour and kernel notes, and then action items.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: Cool. I pushed the bench sheet this morning, link in the chat — it's "poc-novapay-latency-2026-03". Note: some of the runs from last week were mixed because the batcher was using a default max-batch of 8 which skewed p95 at high concurrency.
[00:28] Elena Ruiz: We saw that — p95 spiked when you had mixed short and long seqs.
[00:31] Priya Kapoor: Exactly. So I split tests into uniform sequence buckets (256/512/1024) to get cleaner TTFT and steady-state numbers.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Quick infra note — on 3/22 we had a node that fell into a degraded state during the run, some PCIe resets in the logs, I haven't filtered them out in the sheet yet.
[00:48] Priya Kapoor: Ok we should exclude that run from the baseline. Samir, do you want the cleaned numbers or raw first?
[00:54] Samir Patel: Cleaned if possible. We need to see typical production behavior.
[00:57] Priya Kapoor: Great — I'll mark the degraded runs as NA and re-upload.
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: So high level on TTFT: with fp16 and batcher tuned to max-batch 4, sequence=256, streaming off, we saw median TTFT ~95ms, p95 ~210ms. With streaming enabled TTFT for first token improved ~20-25ms because we bypass some post-processing until stream flush.
[01:22] Elena Ruiz: Wait, streaming improved TTFT? I thought streaming added overhead because of chunking.
[01:26] Priya Kapoor: Good question — depends on where you measure. For us, streaming reduces perceived TTFT because we can emit partial tokens as soon as decoding starts; the pipeline overlap helps. But end-to-end completion time for long responses can be slightly higher if chunking overhead is nontrivial.
[01:40] Alex Chen: Note — users measured perceived latency which is more aligned with time-to-first-token. So streaming might be preferable for interactive UX.
[01:48] Marta Gomez: For our flows we care about TTFT for auth prompts and then full response later, so yes TTFT is most important.
[01:55] Priya Kapoor: On quantization: int8 produced small speedups in steady-state but we observed a TTFT regression ~10-30ms in some kernels because of extra packing/unpacking path. 4-bit quant gave better overall throughput but increased initial setup time on some backends.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: That matches what we saw with the int8 runtime on our infra — warmup cost was non-trivial. Any thoughts on mitigations?
[02:14] Priya Kapoor: A few: persistent KV cache warmup (keep container/VM warm), pre-warm by sending small synthetic prefixes during low traffic windows, or prefer compiler kernels that do fewer plan builds at cold start. We can also pin a kernel family that has lower cold-start cost even if it's slightly slower steady-state.
[02:28] Samir Patel: Can you explain kernel family pinning?
[02:31] Priya Kapoor: Sure. Our runtime picks kernels via a compiler selection path (we use a mix of vendor-optimized and our tuned kernels). Some kernels (eg cutlass-like kernels) have faster per-token throughput but do more JIT/plan work on first use; others (shape-optimized kernels) do minimal first-call planning. You can force an override in the config to prefer low-latency cold-start kernels for interactive flows.
[02:50] Elena Ruiz: Is that a per-model setting?
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: Yes, you can set it per model or per route. For NovaPay's interactive route we'd recommend the low-cold-start profile and enable streaming.
[02:59] Alex Chen: Relatedly, we noticed KV cache hit patterns — when users submit repeated prefixes the KV cache reduces per-token cost dramatically, but there is an initial miss penalty. That's why warmup matters.
[03:11] Jordan Lee: On the 3/22 run PCIe events — could that explain the odd p95 tail?
[03:14] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely, PCIe hiccups will spike tail latency. Please attach the infra logs; we'll re-run without those nodes.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[03:22] Priya Kapoor: I want to call out an artifact: for seq=1024 we saw p50 ~420ms, p95 ~980ms with streaming off; with streaming on TTFT came down to ~160ms but total completion obviously stretched. So if you want low TTFT and can stream partial tokens, streaming wins. If you need atomic full-responses, it's trickier.
[03:38] Samir Patel: For payments flows we need TTFT strong but sometimes we need full responses for legal copy — mixed use. Thoughts?
[03:44] Alex Chen: You can use streaming for interactive confirmation and then run a background non-streamed high-quality pass for the final text, or use function-calling structured outputs to reduce ambiguity. It's a design tradeoff.
[03:55] Elena Ruiz: On compiler/kernel side, you mentioned "triton-like" vs vendor cutlass — we don't have triton in our infra, is it relevant?
[04:02] Priya Kapoor: Sorry that was shorthand — I meant Triton-style custom kernels vs vendor libraries. Even if you don't run Triton, the idea is some kernels are more JIT-heavy. We'll provide recommended kernel map for your target GPU.
[04:12] Marta Gomez: Any impact from sequence bucketing in the batcher?
[04:15] Priya Kapoor: Yes — aggressive bucketing (grouping similar sequence lengths) reduces wasted compute and lowers p95. We recommend dynamic bucketing with a short timeout to avoid latency blowups.
[04:24] Samir Patel: Can the Redwood runtime expose those bucketing settings via the console?
[04:27] Alex Chen: Yes, console will surface batcher config, max-batch, bucketing heuristics, and you can tune per-route. We'll include a suggested baseline.
[04:35] Jordan Lee: Question on Dedicated — if we do Dedicated nodes, do we get persistent warmed kernels?
[04:40] Priya Kapoor: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity so your warm caches and JITs stay resident, which reduces cold-start and TTFT variance. There's still some momentary variance on restarts but far lower.
[04:49] Samir Patel: Pricing rough ballpark for Dedicated?
[04:51] Alex Chen: I'll share a rough estimate in the follow-up email — depends on GPU type and commitment. For this POC baseline, we'll model T4-equivalent vs A10G vs A100 and show per-token economics.
[04:59] Elena Ruiz: Any quick wins to reduce TTFT while staying hosted?
[05:02] Priya Kapoor: For hosted: enable streaming for interactive routes, lower max-batch for those routes, pin low-cold-start kernel family, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and use quantization only after confirming TTFT impact in bench runs.
[05:16] Marta Gomez: Will you include the exact config values?
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: Yes — I'll attach a tuned config snippet with recommended values (max-batch=4, bucket-timeout=15ms, kernel-profile=low-cold-start) in the sheet.
[05:26] Samir Patel: Ok great. A couple of more technical Qs: how do you measure TTFT in your metrics? Our current tracing captures request arrive -> first byte; is that equivalent?
[05:35] Priya Kapoor: That's equivalent — we measure request receive -> first token emitted. We also measure decode latency and RPC overhead separately. We'll share the metric definitions in the sheet.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: For the bench matrix, do you want us to run throughput runs too or just latency?
[05:48] Priya Kapoor: Both. We'll need throughput/escalation points to model cost. But primary focus this week is TTFT and p95 under interactive load.
[05:56] Alex Chen: Quick note — we saw competitor notes where some teams reported TTFT <80ms but only by sacrificing caching and quant; we want to be realistic about tradeoffs.
[06:06] Samir Patel: Understood. Can you also flag any reliability caveats?
[06:10] Priya Kapoor: Sure — high-batch throughput modes are great for cost but increase p95 and can cause head-of-line latency for short requests. Also quantized kernels sometimes show variance across GPUs.
[06:19] Elena Ruiz: Any specific GPU families you recommend for low-TTFT interactive flows?
[06:22] Priya Kapoor: A10G/RTX6000 class are good mid-tier; A100 gives best steady-state but can be overkill cost-wise. Dedicated pilot should test T4/A10/A100 to find sweet spot — we'll help size.
[06:35] Samir Patel: Cool. On the security side — Samir: quick confirmation, Alex, you said you'd share SOC2 addendum?
[06:41] Alex Chen: Yes, I'll attach it with the follow-up. Also we'll include our audit log retention options and KMS integration notes.
[06:48] Marta Gomez: Please include SSO/SAML flow for our engineers.
[06:50] Alex Chen: Will do.
[06:52] Priya Kapoor: Back to bench details — I'll include both streaming chunk sizes and a toggle for emit-early vs buffer-first so you can see the tradeoffs.
[07:00] Jordan Lee: One last infra ask: when you send the tuned config, include a note on container lifecycle so we can ensure containers don't recycle too often.
[07:07] Priya Kapoor: Yep will include restart policies and pre-warm hooks.
[07:10] Alex Chen: Alright let's capture action items — Priya runs the bench matrix and updates the sheet; Jordan attaches infra logs; Alex shares tuned config + pricing + security docs; Samir confirms success criteria. Follow-up call next Wed.
[07:26] Samir Patel: Sounds good, thanks.
[07:28] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll sync next week.

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels are approximate, occasional filler words and minor transcription errors ("cutlass" sometimes noted as "cut-last"), proper nouns may be slightly off in automated text.
